newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Left to talk to Renault on doomed car plant.
newsitem.headline: French Left to talk to Renault on doomed car plant.

text.p: France's newly elected Socialists plan to hold talks with Renault over the carmaker's controversial decision to shut down a car plant in Belgium, party spokesman Francois Hollande said on Monday.

Renault said in February it would close the Vilvoorde plant to streamline its operations, sparking a storm of protest from Belgian trade unions and politicians and prompting the French Socialists to pledge to try to keep it open if they took power.

"The government will engage in the necessary discussions with Renault," Hollande told a news conference on plans for a Socialist-led administration following the French left's win in parliamentary elections on Sunday.
Officials at Renault declined to comment.
French daily newspaper Le Monde on Saturday quoted Socialist leader Lionel Jospin as saying he would ask Renault to look for ways to keep the plant running.
Belgian trade unions were among the first to congratulate Jospin on the left's election victory and called on the new government to honour its promises.
